flow cytometry.readouts: monocyte subset frequencies (CD14+CD16−, CD14+CD16+), intracellular IL-6, TNF-α, and IL-10 percentages in monocytes

evidence_location.quote: We evaluated monocyte populations at each time point, and found induction of CD14+CD16+ monocytes after influenza vaccination, particularly at days 2 and 7 after vaccination, with resolution toward baseline by day 28 (Figure 1); this induction of CD14+CD16+ so-called inflammatory monocytes did not differ between young and older adults (Figure 1B).

hemagglutination inhibition (HAI) assays.readouts: antibody titers against vaccine strains; 4-fold titer increase used to define vaccine responders vs nonresponders

evidence_location.quote: We subsequently classified subjects as influenza vaccine responders (defined as having any 4-fold increase in HAI titer to any of the 3 strains in the vaccine) or nonresponders (having no 4-fold increase in HAI titer to any vaccine strain).

Western blot analysis.sample_type: PBMC lysates and purified monocyte lysates
Western blot analysis.readouts: total STAT3, phosphorylated STAT3 (Y705, S727), total DUSP1, phosphorylated DUSP1 (S296, S359) protein levels

evidence_location.quote: Because both IL-6 and IL-10 signal transduction use STAT3-dependent pathways, we assessed total and p-STAT3 protein in Western blot analyses of PBMC lysates from young and older adults (Figure 4A). In a subset of 14 young and 14 older adults from the original cohort, we found unchanged levels of total STAT3 protein but a significant baseline increase in STAT3 Y705 and S727 phosphorylation in older compared with young subjects (Figure 4B).
